transcript:
Meeting header: Oct 15, 2025 16:00 PT — Duration: ~52 mins — Recording: Local
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortega (Redwood SE), Jesse Park (Redwood AM); Priya Rao (CTO, Oxforda), Dan Whitman (Head ML Infra), Elena Marquez (Finance), Samir Patel (Backend)

Summary: quick budget sanity check, high level architecture mapping, decide whether to start with Hosted pilot or scope Dedicated/Private evaluation; finance wants a hard ceiling and unit-econ scenarios.

Topics: budget lanes, per-token vs per-embed pricing, batching/caching levers, residency and SOC2, pilot scope and benchmarks.

00:00:02 Maya: All right, thanks everyone for joining. This is Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE working with you on the infra side. Quick round robin?
00:00:10 Priya: Hi this is Priya, CTO at Oxforda, we run a search/assistant product across enterprise customers.
00:00:14 Dan: Dan, Head of ML infra. We're focused on costs — like real monthly run rates — and also compliance.
00:00:17 Elena: Elena from finance, I'll be tightly coupling on budget constraints.
00:00:20 Maya: Great. Objective today is a budget sanity check — understand your QPS, latency SLOs, and whether Hosted gets you there or we need Dedicated/Private.

00:01:05 Dan: Quick background: we currently run models on self-managed k8s + Triton for some tasks, but cost has ballooned and ops overhead is high. We're evaluating Redwood for a faster path. Primary constraint: we cannot exceed $120k/month for inference in year one for the pilot footprint.
00:01:26 Elena: To add, that $120k is flexible but we need scenarios — worst case, nominal, optimistic — to present to the board.

00:02:09 Liam: Useful. Two levers we typically look at: software-side (batching, KV cache reuse, prompt compression) and hosting-side (dedicated reserved capacity, burst credits, quantized model variants). For each scenario we map to per-token-ish unit costs.
00:02:24 Priya: Can you unpack per-token vs per-embedding — we use both. Embeddings will be precomputed for many cases, but the assistant path is heavy token generation.
00:02:36 Liam: Sure. Hosted pricing is typically per-token for generation, per-embedding call. Dedicated we model as fixed capacity + lower per-token compute. Private has higher infra capex but predictable monthly cost and data residency. In practice batching + KV cache can cut per-token by 30-70% depending on session reuse.

00:03:15 Samir: When you say KV cache, are you doing prefix cache or whole-session? We've got a bunch of short chats and some long-running sessions.
00:03:21 Liam: We do both — prefix caching and full KV for token reuse. Note, sometimes transcripts show as "K V cash" in older transcriptions — ha — but basically we reduce repeated context cost.

00:04:02 Elena: What's the rough delta between Hosted and Dedicated for the same SLO? Ballpark percent.
00:04:08 Maya: Ballpark, if you're doing a lot of small requests and can't batch: Hosted might be 1.0x baseline. With Dedicated and reserved GPU pools plus batching we often see 35-55% lower per-token compute cost at scale. But that depends on your pattern.
00:04:27 Dan: Our pattern: average payload 160 tokens returned, 60 tokens prompt, peak QPS 12, average QPS 3. Tail latency SLO 99th around 400ms required.
00:04:42 Liam: That distribution helps. Short-ish outputs mean batching matters; with continuous batching and good batching windows we can reduce GPU idle cost. For 12 peak QPS you might fit on a small Dedicated pool depending on concurrency.

00:05:40 Priya: Elena's question re: finance: we need an actual per-month projection with best/worst case. Can you provide example scenarios?
00:05:48 Maya: Yes — we'll send a per-token unit-econ spreadsheet. Example scenarios: Hosted conservative — no caching, baseline model, estimate $140k/month (overshoots your ceiling). Hosted optimized — with batching and caching maybe $90k/month. Dedicated small reserve — $70k/month committed + variable overage; Private on prem — high fixed capex year one but lower variable ops if you amortize.

00:07:02 Elena: That Hosted conservative number worries me. What's driving it to $140k? Is it model choice?
00:07:07 Liam: Mostly model size and lack of reuse. If you insist on a large LLM (20B+) and no quantization, each token costs more. Also embeddings called inline without caching. We'll show swaps: smaller model or 8-bit quantized variant reduces per-token time and cost.

00:07:40 Samir: What about burst credits? We have spiky traffic — billing surprises are a concern.
00:07:46 Maya: We offer burst buckets on Dedicated plans and rate limit windows on Hosted. Mechanically, Dedicated commitment gives you a baseline compute allotment and then burst/overage pricing that is lower than pure Hosted overage. We'll model a spike scenario in the spreadsheet.

00:08:55 Dan: On compliance: to move to Private we need KMS integration, SSO (SAML/Okta), audit logs, and SOC2. Are these available?
00:09:03 Jesse: Yes — Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and SAML SSO; we produce audit logs and can support SOC2 attestations. We'll send the security pack.
00:09:15 Priya: Do you support JIT model updates or CI/CD style model rollouts? We want canary and rollback.
00:09:22 Liam: Yes, canary rollouts and automatic fallback to smaller variants if latency spikes — that's part of our rollout tooling.

00:10:12 Elena: Back to budget: what exact metrics do you need from us to make good scenarios?
00:10:17 Liam: Peak QPS, average QPS, distribution of request sizes (tokens in prompt and output), percent of sessions that are reused (i.e., KV cache hit rate), number of embedding calls per day, SLO targets (p50/p95/p99 latency), and desired residency/compliance constraints.

00:11:25 Priya: For reuse, we think about 45% of requests will hit cache due to repeated prompts. Is that optimistic?
00:11:31 Liam: That's credible. If 45% reuse you can cut hotspots dramatically — we'll model 30%, 45%, 60% hits.

00:12:40 Dan: One more specific: we run a reranking pipeline where we do an embedding search then rerank by generation prompts. That pattern is embedding-heavy plus generation per top-K. How do you charge that?
00:12:50 Liam: Embeddings are charged per-embedding call; if you precompute vector DBs we count only the on-demand calls. For combined patterns we show composite cost lines in the sheet — e.g., embeddings + N generation calls.

00:14:05 Elena: How does quantization affect quality? Our PMs will push back if answers degrade.
00:14:11 Liam: Quality delta depends on model and task. For many NLU and assistant tasks, 8-bit and some 4-bit quant variants are near-parity; for specific generation style nuances there can be regressions. We recommend A/B evals on your prompt set before switching. Redwood Optimize can recommend quant settings per workload.

00:15:33 Priya: Ok, pilot scope. Ideally we'd start 6 weeks, show cost delta and perf, then expand. Suggested structure?
00:15:40 Maya: Typical pilot: 4-8 week trial. Phase 1 (2 weeks) metric collection + baseline on Hosted with your sample traffic; Phase 2 (2-4 weeks) introduce batching, KV cache, smaller quant variant; Phase 3 (optional) test Dedicated reserved config and compare. Pilot SOW + pricing for pilot will be in the doc.

00:16:52 Dan: Curious about latency guarantees. We need 99th <= 400ms. Can Hosted hit that?
00:16:58 Liam: Hosted can for many models, but you trade off cost. Dedicated lets you pin latency by reserving capacity and controlling colocated GPUs; Private same but with on-prem choices. We'll simulate tail behavior in the perf plan.

00:18:05 Elena: About invoicing and commitments — are there monthly commit tiers?
00:18:11 Maya: Yes — Dedicated has monthly/annual committed tiers; Hosted is pay-as-you-go with volume tiers. We can model committed discounts in the spreadsheet.

00:19:20 Priya: Is there an SLA for Hosted?
00:19:24 Jesse: Hosted comes with standard uptime terms; Dedicated and Private have enterprise SLAs with higher availability and faster incident response. We'll include the SLA matrix.

00:21:01 Samir: On benchmarking — will you run a perf test that mimics our pattern?
00:21:06 Liam: We'll run a perf run against a test harness with your token distribution, including cache-hit and miss percentages. We ask you to provide sample prompts and an anonymized dataset for realistic latencies.

00:23:18 Elena: If we model a 50k monthly active users with 5 requests per user per month and your earlier token counts, what's the order of magnitude run rate?
00:23:25 Liam: Quick back-of-envelope: 50k *5 = 250k requests. With average 220 tokens total (prompt+resp) that's 55M tokens/month. Multiply by unit compute and add embeddings — we'll show that concretely. If per-token hosted rate is X, you can estimate.

00:25:00 Priya: Also want to call out data residency — several of our customers insist EU-only. Can Hosted pin region?
00:25:08 Maya: Hosted can be regionally constrained for Enterprise customers; Dedicated/Private gives stronger controls. We'll note region options and data flows in security pack.

00:27:12 Elena: Finance will insist on a 3-scenario view: optimistic (60% cache hit, quantized), base (45% cache hit), conservative (20% cache hit, no quant). Can you deliver all three?
00:27:18 Maya: Yes, we'll produce three rows in the unit-econ sheet with assumptions spelled out.

00:29:33 Dan: One more architecture question: how do you route by policy? For cost we'd like low-value requests to go to smaller models and expensive SLO-sensitive to higher tier.
00:29:41 Liam: Smart routing is supported — you can route by path or token budget and fallback policies. Redwood can auto-fall back to cheaper variants if a model isn't available. We'll add routing examples in the playbook.

00:31:00 Priya: Competitors question — we've looked at Anthropic and BigCloudAI. What is Redwood differentiation here on unit-econ?
00:31:08 Maya: Two big diffs: we optimize serving runtime for batching/kv reuse to push down per-token cost, and we give unified tooling across Hosted/Dedicated/Private so you don't rewrite infra as you move to residency. We'll share benchmark snippets.

00:33:12 Elena: Can we get a binder with assumptions clearly called out? Finance wants transparency: model sizes, quant levels, hit rates, reserved vs burst rentals.
00:33:20 Maya: Absolutely — the spreadsheet will have all assumptions per row.

00:35:55 Samir: For the pilot, storage and egress charges — are embeddings exported to our vector DB charged extra?
00:35:59 Liam: Embeddings API call cost covers generation; storing vectors in your DB is separate cloud egress/storage. We'll highlight that so you can include it in finance model.

00:37:40 Priya: SLO failure scenarios — if Dedicated goes down, can we failover to Hosted?
00:37:46 Liam: Yes — cross-variant fallback is supported. We can route to hosted for critical flows with throttles; plan how to handle burst capacity and cost.

00:39:12 Elena: Any hidden fees? We want predictability.
00:39:16 Maya: We try to avoid surprises. We'll list variable components: overage, egress, storage, on-demand embeddings. We'll recommend a committed tier if you want predictability.

00:41:40 Dan: Technical nit — which GPUs do you surface? H100 or A100? Some of our models are optimized for H100 kernels.
00:41:46 Liam: We support both in Dedicated and Private; Hosted includes a mix but we can arrange H100-backed variants for enterprise pilots. We'll note the perf delta in the test plan.

00:44:02 Priya: Great. Can you summarize what you'll send and timelines?
00:44:08 Maya: Yes — unit-econ spreadsheet with three scenarios (by 10/17), security pack and SOC2 + SAML/KMS notes (by 10/18), perf test plan and 2-hour deep-dive proposed times (by 10/20). After you provide traffic distribution and sample prompts we'll run an initial hosted baseline within 2 weeks.

00:46:20 Elena: We'll also confirm pilot budget ceiling — I think we can go up to $100k if the pilot shows a credible path to $70k committed. I'll confirm via email by 10/22.

00:48:01 Maya: Great, noted. Anything else?
00:48:06 Priya: One ask — show a toggled example where 10% of requests are routed to a cheaper quant variant automatically and show quality delta on a sample prompt set.
00:48:15 Liam: Yup, that's part of the perf/a-b plan.

00:50:00 Maya: Ok, recap — we'll send the sheet, security docs, and performance plan. Priya/Dan you'll share QPS distribution + sample prompts; Elena confirms pilot budget ceiling. We'll reconvene after the perf-deep-dive.
00:50:20 Priya: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
00:50:25 Dan: Thanks.
00:50:28 Elena: Thanks.
00:50:32 Jesse: Thanks, talk soon.

00:51:00 END OF RECORDING

Action items (auto-extract): Maya to send unit-econ scenarios; Liam to draft perf plan; Jesse to share security pack; Customer to share traffic and sample prompts; Finance to confirm ceiling.

Questions (captured during call): What are realistic cache-hit rates? How much does 4-bit quant affect quality? Can Dedicated pinned GPUs guarantee 99th < 400ms?
